paper.title: The Devil is in the Condition Numbers: Why is GLU Better than non-GLU Structure?

fixed_command: uv sync --frozen --no-dev && uv run python -m reproduction.run_suite

claims.exact_statement: kappa(K_tilde)=O(n/d^2) for GLU versus kappa(K)=O(n/d) for non-GLU.
claims.limitation: Finite Monte Carlo corroboration of an asymptotic theorem.

claims.exact_statement: K_tilde is approximated by K Hadamard-multiplied by XX^T/d.
claims.limitation: The source relation is an approximation after dropping small variance terms.

claims.exact_statement: GLU contracts lambda_max by an extra d factor while both lambda_min scale as O(m).
Under Gaussian inputs, d>=5, n>=300, d+1<n and nonnegative Y^T(K-K_tilde)Y, expected losses cross between early and sufficiently late optimization.
claims.limitation: Expected-kernel finite numerical evaluation; not a universal proof.

claims.exact_statement: GLU's primary benefit is optimization acceleration rather than a materially smaller generalization gap in the considered real-model experiments.
claims.why_blocked: The full-data run used dim=64/depth=2 for 15 epochs instead of the source-default dim=256/depth=4 for 100 epochs. It verifies the limited-gap component but neither verifies acceleration nor supplies an assumption-complete falsification.

claims.exact_statement: Parameter-matched GLU FFNs have lower empirical NTK condition numbers in ViT and GPT-2.
claims.limitation: n=8 rather than the official ViT script's n=64; GPT-2 was independently reconstructed because the official release has no GPT-2 NTK code.
